correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 and 0<tau<1, the exact uncovered phase fraction is a sum of positive parts of cyclic gaps. Convexity gives a pointwise optimal bound attained by equal gaps. The equality classification follows by considering arc lengths approaching average gap pi/n and, in the complete regime, the smallest arc length. Integration by parts yields the exact elementary completeness expression. The explicit integral with positive integrand establishes the boundary and 3/2 exponent, and the standalone checker completed 577 supporting assertions. No numerical finite test is used to establish an all-n claim.

value.rationale: For a fixed known-period circular orbit, the theorem gives the exact minimum number of geometrically sufficient observations and all cadence calendars attaining maximum visibility. It distinguishes a unique rigid optimum below complete coverage from a family of feasible calendars above it, which changes practical scheduling flexibility, and provides a closed-form sensitivity benchmark for realistic simulations. The result has a specific observer-facing use despite idealized separation-only detectability; full mission modeling is outside scope.
